questions.question: Summarize the objectives of the Information Technology Act, 2000.
questions.solution_html:
• Objectives of IT Act, 2000
  • • Legal recognition of electronic records and signatures
  • • Promotion of e-governance
  • • Prevention of cyber crimes
  • • Facilitation of electronic commerce
  • Malicious code attacks (virus, trojan, worms)

questions.question: Explain the role of Cyber Laws in controlling digital activities.
questions.solution_html:
• Role of Cyber Laws in controlling digital activities
  • Cyber laws regulate digital behavior by
  • • Defining cyber crimes and punishments
  • • Protecting data and privacy
  • • Regulating e-commerce transactions
  • • Ensuring safe online communication
  • • Supporting cyber security enforcement agencies
  • They help maintain order, security, and trust in cyberspace.
questions.final_answer: They help maintain order, security, and trust in cyberspace
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Write the adjudication process under the IT Act.
questions.solution_html:
• Adjudication process under IT Act
  • • Appointment of Adjudicating Officer
  • • Inquiry into cyber offence or negligence
  • • Giving opportunity to both parties
  • • Determining compensation/penalty
  • • Orders passed based on evidence
  • Appeal lies to Cyber Appellate Tribunal (now TDSAT).
questions.final_answer: Appeal lies to Cyber Appellate Tribunal (now TDSAT)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Write a short note on the Yahoo! data breach and explain why it is / considered one of the largest in history.
questions.solution_html:
• Yahoo data breach
  • The Yahoo breach (2013–2014) affected over 3 billion accounts.
  • • Stolen data: emails, passwords, personal details
  • • Caused by unauthorized access and hacking
  • • Considered largest breach due to scale
  • • Resulted in lawsuits and reduced trust in Yahoo
questions.final_answer: • Resulted in lawsuits and reduced trust in Yahoo
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Appraise the lessons learned from high-profile cyber crime cases for / future prevention.
questions.solution_html:
• Lessons from high-profile cyber crime cases
  • • Strong encryption is essential
  • • Regular security audits are needed
  • • Employee awareness reduces risks
  • • Companies must detect breaches early
  • • Strict data protection laws are necessary
questions.final_answer: • Strict data protection laws are necessary
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What was the legal dispute between Amazon and its third-party sellers / over counterfeit products.Explain how it was resolved.
questions.solution_html:
• Amazon and counterfeit seller dispute
  • • Issue: Sale of counterfeit goods by third-party sellers
  • • Amazon faced criticism for lack of control
  • • Resolution
  • o Introduction of Brand Registry
  • o Strict seller verification
  • o AI-based counterfeit detection
  • Improved protection for genuine sellers and buyers

questions.question: Illustrate the provisions relating to E-Governance and electronic records / under the IT Act, 2000 using governmental service delivery examples.
questions.solution_html:
• E-Governance and electronic records under IT Act
  • E-Governance provisions
  • • Section 6: Electronic filing of documents with government
  • • Section 7: Retention of electronic records
  • • Section 8: Publication in electronic form
  • • Section 9: No right to insist on paper format
  • Examples
  • • Online income tax filing
  • • Passport Seva portal
  • • DigiLocker services
  • • GST portal
  • Importance
  • • Faster service delivery
  • • Reduced paperwork
  • • Transparency in administration
  • • Cost efficiency

questions.question: Evaluate the impact of modern technologies such as social media, AI, / and cloud computing on individual privacy rights.
questions.solution_html:
• Impact of modern technologies on privacy rights
  • Social Media
  • • Excess data sharing
  • • Tracking user behavior
  • • Risk of identity theft
  • Artificial Intelligence
  • • Facial recognition surveillance
  • • Data profiling without consent
  • • Algorithmic bias affecting privacy
  • Cloud Computing
  • • Data stored on remote servers
  • • Risk of data breaches
  • • Dependency on third-party providers
  • Overall impact
  • • Privacy becomes harder to protect
  • • Need for strong laws like Digital Personal Data Protection Act
  • • Users must be aware of digital footprints
questions.final_answer: • Users must be aware of digital footprints
